column1: # GreyIQ wardrive — curated IEEE MA-L (OUI) subset.
# vintage: 2026-07  |  provenance: hand-curated from the public IEEE MA-L registry
# scope: DELIBERATELY NOT the full ~35k-row registry. Only prefixes that can CHANGE A
#   VERDICT during rogue-AP / evil-twin triage are carried:
#     enterprise-ap  — vendors whose kit is normally part of a managed WLAN
#     consumer-ap    — retail / ISP CPE, i.e. "someone plugged in their own router"
#     soc-devboard   — SoC and dev-board makers; a BEACONING AP on one of these prefixes
#                      in a corporate RF environment is inherently worth a look
#     mobile         — handset/laptop radios, so a client looks like a client
#     network-gear   — switching/routing silicon that also ships radios
# HONESTY CONTRACT: a BSSID that is ABSENT from this table means "not in GreyIQ's
# curated subset", NOT "unknown vendor" and NEVER "suspicious". oui.vendor_for()
# returns None for it and the report prints the table's vintage next to every
# unknown-vendor verdict so table age is attributable rather than presented as fact.
# The zero-byte, always-correct signal that needs no table at all is the
# phone-hotspot signature that works on every address, in or out of this file.
